title: AWS S3: SignatureDoesNotMatch on object keys containing "=" or ":" (path signed un-encoded, sent percent-encoded) — regression in 2.31.5
user_goal: Download S3 objects whose keys contain equals signs or colons.
obstacle: n8n signs an unencoded path but sends a percent-encoded path, producing SignatureDoesNotMatch.
workaround: Percent-encode each key segment and use an HTTP Request node with an AWS credential and a path-style S3 URL.
human_cost: Fragile custom URL construction that will break through double encoding after the signer is fixed.
underlying_need: AWS signing over the same canonical path that n8n transmits.
opportunity_statement: Users need a better way to Download S3 objects whose keys contain equals signs or colons. without having to Percent-encode each key segment and use an HTTP Request node with an AWS credential and a path-style S3 URL..
evidence_quote: Percent-encode the key per path segment and fetch via HTTP Request + AWS credential over a path-style URL.

human_cost: Dependency on a separate community package and additional maintenance.

opportunity_statement: Users need a better way to Run LDAP searches in production. without having to Install and use the community n8n-nodes-ldap package until upgrading fixes the built-in node..
evidence_quote: But in prod environment only n8n-nodes-ldap@0.1.10 works on Windows Server 2022 Standard.

title: OAuth consent fails with "Invalid or expired authorization session" - n8n-oauth-session cookie hardcoded with Secure attribute ignoring N8N_SECURE_COOKIE=false
user_goal: Complete MCP OAuth consent on an HTTP-hosted n8n instance.
obstacle: The OAuth session cookie is always marked Secure and is dropped on plain HTTP.
workaround: Place n8n behind an HTTPS reverse proxy.
human_cost: Requires extra infrastructure and configuration that should be unnecessary when secure cookies are disabled.
opportunity_statement: Users need a better way to Complete MCP OAuth consent on an HTTP-hosted n8n instance. without having to Place n8n behind an HTTPS reverse proxy..
evidence_quote: Confirmed workaround: putting n8n behind an HTTPS reverse proxy (e.g. Caddy) resolves the issue immediately.

user_goal: Use an imported workflow with its assigned credentials.

workaround: Open and close each affected node so n8n reselects a credential of the same type.
human_cost: Repetitive manual work and uncertainty about whether credentials are actually valid.
underlying_need: Correct credential-state reconciliation immediately after workflow import.
opportunity_statement: Users need a better way to Use an imported workflow with its assigned credentials. without having to Open and close each affected node so n8n reselects a credential of the same type..
evidence_quote: If the user opens an affected node in the node dialog (NDV) and closes it without changing anything, the warning disappears.

title: Postgres workflow statistics rollup crashes when firstEvent is returned as a non-Date value
user_goal: Keep workflow-statistics rollups completing without crashing the container.
obstacle: PostgreSQL can return firstEvent as a string while the code assumes a Date.
workaround: Build and run a custom n8n image with firstEvent normalised through new Date().
human_cost: Engineering effort and ongoing maintenance of a custom image.
underlying_need: Native timestamp normalisation and a regression test in n8n.
opportunity_statement: Users need a better way to Keep workflow-statistics rollups completing without crashing the container. without having to Build and run a custom n8n image with firstEvent normalised through new Date()..
evidence_quote: We applied this change to a custom image based on n8n 2.31.4 and verified it.
